name: Pioneer 0 (Able I)
note: First attempted launch beyond Earth orbit; failed to orbit due to turbopump gearbox malfunction resulting in first-stage explosion. Reached apogee of 16 kilometres (10 mi).

name: Luna E-1 No.1
note: Failed to orbit; rocket disintegrated due to excessive vibration.

name: Pioneer 1 (Able II)
note: Failed to orbit; premature second-stage cutoff due to accelerometer failure. Later known as Pioneer 1. Reached apogee of 113,800 kilometres (70,700 mi).

name: Luna E-1 No.2
note: Failed to orbit; carrier rocket exploded due to excessive vibration.

name: Pioneer 2 (Able III)
note: Failed to orbit; premature second-stage cutoff due to erroneous command by ground controllers; third stage failed to ignite due to broken electrical connection. Reached apogee of 1,550 kilometres (960 mi).

name: Luna E-1 No.3
note: Failed to orbit; seal failure in hydrogen peroxide pump cooling system resulted in core-stage underperformance.

name: Pioneer 3
note: Failed to orbit; premature first-stage cutoff. Reached apogee of 102,360 kilometres (63,600 mi).

name: Luna 1 (E-1 No.4)
note: Carrier rocket guidance problem resulted in failure to impact Moon, flew past in a heliocentric orbit. Closest approach 5,995 kilometres (3,725 mi) on 4 January. First spacecraft to fly by the Moon.

name: Pioneer 4
note: Second-stage overperformance resulted in flyby at greater altitude than expected, out of instrument range, with 58,983 kilometres (36,650 mi) of distance. Closest approach at 22:25 UTC on 4 March. First U.S. spacecraft to leave Earth orbit.

name: E-1A No.1
note: Failed to orbit; guidance system malfunction.

name: Luna 2 (E-1A No.2)
note: Successful impact at 21:02 on 14 September 1959. First spacecraft to impact the lunar surface. This made the Soviet Union the first country to impact the surface of the Moon.

name: Luna 3 (E-2A No.1)
note: Returned the first images of the far side of the Moon.

name: Pioneer P-3 Able IVB
note: Failed to orbit; payload fairing disintegrated due to design fault.

name: Luna E-3 No.1
note: Failed to orbit; premature third-stage cutoff.

name: Luna E-3 No.2
note: Failed to orbit; rocket disintegrated ten seconds after launch.

name: Pioneer P-30 (Able VA)
note: Failed to orbit; second-stage oxidizer system malfunction resulting in premature cutoff.

name: Pioneer P-31 (Able VB)
note: Failed to orbit, exploded 68 seconds after launch, at an altitude of 12.2 kilometres (7.6 mi). Second stage ignited while first stage was still attached and burning.

name: Ranger 3 (P-34)
note: Partial launch failure due to guidance problem; attempt to correct using spacecraft's engine resulted in it missing the Moon by 36,793 kilometres (22,862 mi).

name: Ranger 4 (P-35)
note:
Failed to deploy solar panels, ran out of power ten hours after launch; incidental impact on the far side of the Moon on 26 April. First spacecraft to impact the far side of the Moon.
The impact made the United States the 2nd country to impact the surface of t

name: Luna E-6 No.2
note: Failed to depart Low Earth orbit; guidance system power failure prevented upper-stage ignition.

name: Luna E-6 No.3
note: Failed to orbit; guidance failure.

name: Luna 4 (E-6 No.4)
note: Failed to perform mid-course correction, remained in high Earth orbit until given escape velocity by orbital perturbation.

name: Ranger 6 (P-54)
note: Impacted on 2 February 1964, failed to return images due to power system failure.

name: Luna E-6 No.6
note: Failed to orbit; third stage underperformed due to oxidiser valve failure.

name: Luna E-6 No.5
note: Failed to orbit; power failure caused by broken connection resulted in premature third-stage cutoff.

name: Ranger 7
note: Impacted on 30 July 1964 at 13:25:48 UTC.

name: Ranger 8
note: Impacted on 20 February 1965 at 09:57:37 UTC.

name: Kosmos 60 (E-6 No.9)
note: Upper stage failed to restart due to guidance system short circuit, Failed to depart low Earth orbit.

name: Ranger 9
note: Impacted on 24 March 1965 at 14:08:20 UTC.

name: Luna E-6 No.8
note: Third stage failed to ignite due to loss of oxidiser pressure, failed to orbit.

name: Luna 5 (E-6 No.10)
note: Loss of control after gyroscope malfunction, failed to decelerate for landing and impacted the Moon at 19:10 UTC on 12 May 1965.

name: Luna 6 (E-6 No.7)
note: Engine failed to shut down after performing mid-course correction manoeuvre, flew past the Moon in a heliocentric orbit.

name: Zond 3 (3MV-4 No.3)
note: Flew past the Moon on 20 July 1965 at a distance of 9,200 kilometres (5,700 mi). Conducted technology demonstration for future planetary missions.

name: Luna 7 (E-6 No.11)
note: Attitude control failure shortly before landing prevented controlled descent; impacted the lunar surface 22:08:24 UTC on 7 October 1965.

name: Luna 8 (E-6 No.12)
note: Landing airbag punctured, resulting in loss of attitude control shortly before planned touchdown, impacted Moon on 6 December 1965 at 21:51:30 UTC.

name: Luna 9 (E-6 No.13)
note: First spacecraft to land successfully on the Moon. Touchdown on 3 February 1966 at 18:45:30 UTC. Returned data until 6 February at 22:55 UTC. With its soft landing, the Soviet Union became the first country to successfully land on the lunar surface.

name: Kosmos 111 (E-6S No.204)
note: Upper stage lost attitude control and failed to ignite; spacecraft never left low Earth orbit.

name: Luna 10 (E-6S No.206)
note: Entered orbit at 18:44 UTC on 3 April 1966, becoming the first spacecraft to orbit the Moon. Continued to return data until 30 May.

name: Surveyor 1
note: Landed in Oceanus Procellarum on 2 June 1966 at 06:17:36 UTC. Returned data until loss of power on 13 July. With its soft landing, the United States became the second country to successfully land on the lunar surface.

name: Explorer 33 (AIMP-D)
note: Magnetospheric probe; rocket imparted greater velocity than had been planned, leaving spacecraft unable to enter orbit. Repurposed for Earth orbit mission which was completed successfully.

name: Lunar Orbiter 1
note: Orbital insertion at around 15:36 UTC on 14 August. Deorbited early due to lack of fuel and to avoid communications interference with the next mission, impacted the Moon at 13:30 UTC on 29 October 1966.

name: Luna 11 (E-6LF No.101)
note: Entered orbit on 28 August 1966. Failed to return images; other instruments operated correctly. Conducted gamma ray and X-ray observations to study the composition of the Moon, investigated the lunar gravitational field, the presence of meteorites in the lunar

name: Surveyor 2
note: One thruster failed to ignite during mid-course correction manoeuvre, resulting in loss of control. Impacted the Moon at 03:18 UTC on 23 September 1966.

name: Luna 12 (E-6LF No.102)
note: Entered orbit on 25 October 1966 and returned data until 19 January 1967. Completed photography mission intended for Luna 11.

name: Lunar Orbiter 2
note: Entered orbit at about 19:51 UTC on 10 November 1966 to begin photographic mapping mission. Impacted on the far side of the lunar surface following deorbit burn on 11 October 1967 at end of mission.

name: Luna 13 (E-6M No.205)
note: Successfully landed in Oceanus Procellarum at 18:01 UTC on 24 December 1966. Returned images from the surface and studied the lunar soil. Operated until depletion of power at 06:31 UTC on 28 December.

name: Lunar Orbiter 3
note: Entered orbit at 21:54 UTC on 8 February 1967. Deorbited at end of mission and impacted the Moon on 9 October 1967.

name: Surveyor 3
note: Landed at 00:04 UTC on 20 April 1967 and operated until 3 May. Visited by Apollo 12 astronauts in 1969, with some parts removed for return to Earth.

name: Lunar Orbiter 4
note: Entered orbit at 21:54 UTC on 8 May 1967, operated until 17 July. Decayed from orbit, with lunar impact occurring on 6 October 1967.

name: Surveyor 4
note: Contact with spacecraft lost at 02:03 UTC on 17 July, two and a half minutes before scheduled landing. NASA determined that the spacecraft may have exploded, otherwise it impacted the Moon.

name: Explorer 35(AIMP-E)
note: Magnetospheric probe, studying the Moon and interplanetary space. Deactivated on 27 June 1973. Presumed to have impacted the Moon during the 1970s.

name: Lunar Orbiter 5
note: Final mission in the Lunar Orbiter series, entered selenocentric orbit on 5 August at 16:48 UTC and conducted a photographic survey until 18 August. Deorbited and impacted the Moon on 31 January 1968.

name: Surveyor 5
note: Landed in Mare Tranquillitatis at 00:46:44 UTC on 11 September. Last signals received at 04:30 UTC on 17 December 1967.

name: Soyuz 7K-L1 No.4L
note: Technology demonstration for planned crewed missions. Failed to reach orbit after a blocked propellant line caused one of the first-stage engines to not ignite.

name: Surveyor 6
note: Landed in Sinus Medii at 01:01:04 UTC on 10 November. Made brief flight from lunar surface at 10:32 UTC on 17 November, followed by second landing after travelling 2.4 metres (7 ft 10 in). Last contact at 19:14 UTC on 14 December.

name: Soyuz 7K-L1 No.5L
note: Technology demonstration for planned crewed missions; unable to achieve orbit after second-stage engine failed to ignite.

name: Surveyor 7
note: Final Surveyor mission. Landed 29 kilometres (18 mi) from Tycho crater at 01:05:36 UTC on 10 January. Operated until 21 February 1968.

name: Luna E-6LS No.112
note: Failed to orbit after third stage ran out of fuel.

name: Luna 14 (E-6LS No.113)
note: Tested communications for proposed crewed missions and studied the mass concentration of the Moon. Entered orbit on 10 April at 19:25 UTC.

name: Soyuz 7K-L1 No.7L
note: Technology demonstration for planned crewed missions. Failed to orbit after second-stage engine incorrectly commanded to shut down. Spacecraft was recovered using its prototype launch escape system.

name: Zond 5 (7K-L1 No.9L)
note: Two tortoises and other life forms on board a technology demonstration for planned crewed missions. Made a closest approach of 1,950 kilometres (1,210 mi) on 18 September, and circled the Moon before returning to Earth. Landed in the Indian Ocean on 21 Septemb

name: Zond 6 (7K-L1 No.12L)
note: Technology demonstration for planned crewed missions. Carrying turtles, making this the second mission of Earthlings to travel in close proximity of the Moon, the flyby was on 14 November with a closest approach of 2,420 kilometres (1,500 mi). Reentered Earth'

name: Apollo 8
note: First crewed mission to the Moon; entered orbit around the Moon with four-minute burn beginning at 09:59:52 UTC on 24 December. Completed ten orbits of the Moon and presented a reading from the Book of Genesis before returning to Earth with an engine burn at 0

name: Soyuz 7K-L1 No.13L
note: Technology demonstration for planned crewed missions. Failed to orbit after one of the four second-stage engines shut down prematurely. Third-stage engine also shut down prematurely. The spacecraft was recovered using its launch escape system.

name: Luna E-8 No.201
note: First launch of the Lunokhod rover. Launch vehicle disintegrated 51 seconds after launch and exploded.

name: Soyuz 7K-L1S No.3
note: First launch of N1 rocket; intended to orbit the Moon and return to Earth. First stage prematurely shut down 70 seconds after launch; launch vehicle crashed 50 kilometres (31 mi) from launch site. Spacecraft landed some 35 kilometres (22 mi) from the launch pa

name: Apollo 10
note: Dress rehearsal for Apollo 11. Lunar Module with two astronauts on board descended to a distance of 14.326 kilometres (8.902 mi) above the lunar surface.

name: Luna E-8-5 No.402
note: Intended to land on the Moon and return lunar soil sample. Did not reach Earth orbit after fourth stage failed to ignite.

name: Soyuz 7K-L1S No.5
note: Intended to orbit the Moon and return to Earth. All first-stage engines shut down 10 seconds after launch; launch vehicle crashed and exploded on the launch pad. Spacecraft landed safely 2 kilometres (1.2 mi) from the launch site after using launch escape sequ

name: Luna 15 (E-8-5 No.401)
note: Reached lunar orbit at 10:00 UTC on 17 July. Descent retro-rocket burn started at 15:47 UTC on 21 July. Contact lost three minutes after de-orbit burn; probably crashed on the Moon.

name: Apollo 11
note: First crewed landing on the Moon. The Lunar Module Eagle landed at 20:17 UTC on 20 July 1969.

name: Zond 7 (7K-L1 No.11L)
note: Technology demonstration for planned crewed missions. Carried four turtles in a lunar flyby on 10 August, with a closest approach of 1,200 kilometres (750 mi); returned to Earth and landed in Kazakhstan at 18:13 UTC on 14 August.

name: Kosmos 300 (E-8-5 No.403)
note: Third attempt at lunar sample return. After reaching low Earth orbit, the fourth-stage engine failed to fire for trans-lunar injection due to oxidizer leak. Spacecraft re-entered Earth's atmosphere about 4 days after launch.

name: Kosmos 305 (E-8-5 No.404)
note: Fourth attempt at lunar sample return. After reaching low Earth orbit, the fourth-stage engine failed to fire for trans-lunar injection due to control system malfunction. Spacecraft re-entered Earth's atmosphere within one orbit after launch.

name: Apollo 12
note: Second crewed lunar landing.

name: Luna E-8-5 No.405
note: Failed to orbit

name: Apollo 13
note: Lunar landing aborted following Service Module oxygen tank explosion en route to the Moon; flew past the Moon (free-return trajectory) and returned the crew safely to Earth.

name: Luna 16 (E-8-5 No.406)
note: First robotic sampling mission.

name: Zond 8 (7K-L1 No.14L)
note: Technology demonstration for planned crewed missions; returned to Earth successfully.

name: Luna 17 (E-8 No.203)
note: Luna 17 deployed Lunokhod 1.

name: Apollo 14
note: Third crewed lunar landing.

name: Apollo 15
note: Fourth crewed lunar landing, and first to use the Lunar Roving Vehicle.

name: PFS-1
note: PFS-1 was deployed from Apollo 15.

name: Luna 18 (E-8-5 No.407)
note: Failed during descent to lunar surface.

name: Luna 19 (E-8LS No.202)
note: Entered an orbit around the Moon on 2 October 1971 after two midcourse corrections on 29 September and 1 October.

name: Luna 20 (E-8-5 No.408)
note: Luna 20 soft landed on the Moon in a mountainous area known as the Terra Apollonius (or Apollonius highlands) near Mare Fecunditatis (Sea of Fertility), 120 km from where Luna 16 had landed.

name: Apollo 16
note: 5th crewed lunar landing.

name: PFS-2
note: PFS-2 deployed from Apollo 16.

name: Soyuz 7K-LOK No.1
note: Failed to orbit; intended to orbit the Moon and return to Earth.

name: Apollo 17
note: Sixth and last crewed Apollo lunar landing and last use of the Lunar Roving Vehicle; the orbiting command module included five mice.

name: Luna 21 (E-8 No.204)
note: Deployed Lunokhod 2.

name: Explorer 49 (RAE-B)
note: Radio astronomy spacecraft, operated in selenocentric orbit to avoid interference from terrestrial radio sources.

name: Mariner 10
note: Interplanetary spacecraft, mapped lunar north pole to test cameras.

name: Luna 22 (E-8LS No.206)
note: Inserted into a circular lunar orbit on 2 June 1974

name: Luna 23 (E-8-5M No.410)
note: Tipped over upon landing, precluding any sample return attempt. Functioned for three days on surface.

name: Luna E-8-5M No.412
note: Failed to orbit.

name: Luna 24 (E-8-5M No.413)
note: Entered orbit on 11 August 1976 and landed in Mare Crisium at 16:36 UTC on 18 August. Sample capsule launched at 05:25 UTC on 19 August and recovered 96+1⁄2 hours later. Returned 170.1 grams (6.00 oz) of lunar regolith. Final mission to the Moon from the Sovie

name: ISEE-3 (ICE/Explorer 59)
note: Five flybys in 1982 and 1983 en route to comet 21P/Giacobini–Zinner.

name: Geotail
note: Series of flybys to regulate high Earth orbit.

name: WIND
note: Made two flybys on 1 December 1994 and 27 December 1994 to reach the Earth–Sun L1 Lagrangian point.

name: Clementine (DSPSE)
note: Completed Lunar objectives successfully; failed following departure from selenocentric orbit.

name: HGS-1
note: Communications satellite; made two flybys in May and June 1998 en route to geosynchronous orbit after delivery into wrong orbit.

name: Lunar Prospector (Discovery 3)
note: The mission ended on July 31, 1999

name: Nozomi (PLANET-B)
note: Two flybys en route to Mars.

name: WMAP
note: Flyby on 30 July 2001 to reach the Earth–Sun L2 Lagrangian point.

name: SMART-1
note: Impacted Moon in USGS quadrangle LQ26 at end of mission on 3 September 2006. The impact made the ESA member states collectively the 4th to impact the surface of the Moon.

name: STEREO
note: Both component spacecraft entered heliocentric orbit on 15 December 2006.

name: ARTEMIS
note: Two THEMIS spacecraft moved to selenocentric orbit for extended mission; entered orbit July 2011.

name: SELENE
note: Deployed Okina and Ouna satellites. Kaguya and Okina impacted the Moon at end of mission. Ouna completed operations on 29 June 2009 but remains in selenocentric orbit.

name: Chang'e 1
note: Impacted Moon in USGS quadrangle LQ21 on 1 March 2009, at end of mission. The impact made China the 5th country and 6th as an agency to impact the surface of the Moon.

name: Chandrayaan-1

name: LRO & LCROSS
note: LCROSS observed impact of Centaur upper stage that launched it and LRO, then impacted itself. Impacts in USGS quadrangle LQ30. LRO entered orbit on June 23, 2009.

name: Chang'e 2

name: GRAIL
note: Impacted the Moon in USGS quadrangle LQ01 on 17 December 2012 at end of mission.

name: LADEE
note: Mission ended on 18 April 2014, when the spacecraft's controllers intentionally crashed LADEE into the far side of the Moon.

name: Chang'e 3
note: Entered orbit on 6 December 2013 with landing at 13:12 UTC on 14 December. Yutu rover was deployed from Chang'e 3. With its soft landing, China became the third country to successfully land on the lunar surface.

name: Chang'e 5-T1
note: Demonstration of re-entry capsule for Chang'e 5 sample-return mission at lunar return velocity. Orbiter may still be in lunar orbit. Manfred Memorial Moon Mission attached to third stage of CZ-3C used to launch Chang'e 5-T1. Impacted the Moon on 4 March 2022.

name: TESS
note: Flyby on 17 May 2018 to designated high Earth orbit.

name: Queqiao
note: Launched on the same rocket as Queqiao. Longjiang-1 never entered Moon orbit, while Longjiang-2 operated in lunar orbit until 31 July 2019, when it impacted the lunar surface. Queqiao entered designated Earth–Moon L2 orbit on 14 June in preparation of Chang'e

name: Chang'e 4
note: First spacecraft to soft land on the far side of the Moon (South Pole–Aitken basin). Landed 3 January 2019 and deployed the Yutu-2 rover. Cottonseeds sprouted in the lander in a biological experiment, the first plants to sprout on the Moon.

name: Beresheet
note: First Israeli and first privately funded lunar lander mission. Technology demonstration. Instrumentation included a magnetometer and laser retroreflector. Spacecraft crashed into the lunar surface after main engine failure during descent from lunar orbit phase

name: Chandrayaan-2
note: Entered orbit on 20 August 2019. Lander separated from orbiter but crashed during a landing attempt on 6 September 2019, attributed to a software glitch. Both lander and rover were lost. Orbiter remained operational.

name: Chang'e 5
note: First lunar sample return mission from China, which returned 1.731 kg (61.1 oz) of lunar samples on 16 December 2020. The orbiter received a mission extension and is currently in a distant retrograde orbit (DRO) of the Moon.

name: CAPSTONE
note: Lunar orbiting CubeSat that will test and verify the calculated orbital stability planned for the Gateway space station.

name: Danuri

name: Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer
note: Flew by the Moon on 19 August 2024 en route to Jupiter.

name: Luna 25
note: Launched on 10 August 2023, Orbital insertion on 16 August 2023, failed orbital maneuver on 19 August 2023 set the spacecraft on the crash course with the Moon's surface. Loss of communication was confirmed by Roscosmos on 20 August 2023.

name: SLIM
note: Launched alongside XRISM as a co-passenger on 7 September 2023. Performed lunar swing-by, followed by lunar orbital insertion on 25 December 2023. SLIM landed intact and within 100 m of its target on 19 January 2024, 15:20 UTC, which met JAXA's criteria for a

name: Peregrine Mission One
note: Part of CLPS. Peregrine lander's reaction thrusters' leak deemed the spacecraft uncontrollable for landing and it decayed in the Earth's atmosphere 10 days later.

name: IM-1
note: First Nova-C mission. First private spacecraft to soft land on the Moon. Payloads successfully delivered for NASA CLPS and for private customers. Though it landed successfully, one of the lander's legs broke upon landing and it tilted up on other side, 18° due

name: Queqiao-2
note: Relay satellite to support future missions of the Chinese Lunar Exploration Program targeting south pole region. Tiandu satellites are launched with them to test communications for future lunar satellite constellation technologies.

name: Chang'e 6

name: Blue Ghost M1
note: Lunar lander, carrying NASA-sponsored experiments and commercial payloads to Mare Crisium. First fully-successful private lunar landing.

name: Hakuto-R Mission 2
note: Launched on the same rocket as Blue Ghost. On 5 June 2025, the lander failed to complete its landing, impacting the lunar surface.

name: Lunar Trailblazer
note: Lunar orbiter aimed to aid in the understanding of lunar water and the Moon's water cycle. Flyby on 3 March 2025.

name: Brokkr-2
note: Asteroid probe intended to flyby the near-Earth asteroid 2022 OB5. Communication failure. Flyby on 3 March 2025.

name: Chimera-1
note: Space tug planned TLI to Geosynchronous. Communication failure?. Flyby on 3 March 2025.

name: IM-2
outcome: Partial failure / Precluded / Precluded / Precluded / Precluded
note: Second Nova-C. Payloads delivery for NASA's CLPS and for private customers. MAPP and μNova were to test a new Nokia lunar communication system. Lander achieved a soft landing on 6 March but landed on its side, precluding recharging and deployment of payloads.

name: Artemis II
note: Crewed test of the Orion spacecraft on a free-return trajectory around the Moon.
